description: Replace the rejected conversation Attempt with the smallest functional privacy-safe implementation and defer conservative sub-millisecond consent precision to hardening.

tasks.title: Deliver private conversation with fail-closed disclosure normalization
tasks.spec: Implement a fresh functional conversation capability from the exact accepted FOUND-BASELOCK-001 SHA without merging or cherry-picking CONV-001, CONV-REPAIR-001, CONV-REPAIR-002, CONV-REPAIR-003, or any rejected Attempt. Preserve the working behavior independently proven in CONV-REPAIR-003: pre-provider authorization of the active actor, space, private message, evidence ownership and state, and same-speaker analysis consent; deterministic provider bypass for every frozen high-risk category; bounded allowlisted provider inputs; recursive inspection of every provider-derived string and nested value; transaction-before-Clock.now confirmation with locked rereads and conditional persistence; self-only raw evidence and private message reads; and content-free logs and errors. Use a version-fixed complete Unicode Default Full Case Folding table. After NFKC and full folding, derive a symmetric disclosure skeleton that removes Unicode marks, punctuation, symbols, separators, controls, and format characters before equality, containment, and one-code-point-edit checks. This must fail closed for repeated internal whitespace, punctuation, and symbol insertion, including STRASSE      family detail, S.T.R.A.S.S.E family detail, and STRASSE ★ ★ ★ family detail against Straße family detail in both directions. Keep the existing general Clock Date boundary for MVP compatibility. Its conservative sub-millisecond consent refusal is a documented non-leaking limitation assigned to CONV-002 hardening; it must never turn an expired or unauthorized consent into an accepted write.
acceptance: The task starts from the exact accepted FOUND-BASELOCK-001 SHA and no rejected Attempt SHA is an ancestor
The private-message to provider-draft to explicit-confirmation user flow works through public module ports
Unauthorized, inactive, cross-space, missing, or mismatched source input fails before provider invocation and provider call count remains zero
Self-harm, domestic-violence, and acute-medical fixtures bypass the provider and create no ordinary task or automatic shared signal
Every provider-derived string and nested value plus the final rendered draft and shared signal is disclosure-checked
The implementation uses version-fixed complete Unicode Default Full Case Folding rather than uppercase or lowercase heuristics
Straße, STRAẞE, and STRASSE plus repeated whitespace, punctuation, symbol, separator, containment, and one-edit variants fail closed in both directions

The real provider pipeline returns needs_human_review and writes nothing for STRASSE      family detail, S.T.R.A.S.S.E family detail, and STRASSE ★ ★ ★ family detail when the protected source contains Straße family detail
Creating a private message produces no shared signal, task, report fact, confirmation record, or cross-role query result
Consent remains same-speaker, present, unexpired, and unrevoked through transaction-safe confirmation
Raw-evidence and private-message queries remain self-only even when another role guesses an identifier
Consent revocation, evidence invalidation, actor deactivation, visibility drift, or version drift during provider execution or before persistence yields zero shared writes
Invalid output, synchronous or asynchronous provider failure, timeout, and a second invalid output return needs_human_review without consequential mutation
The documented sub-millisecond Date limitation can only reject conservatively and is assigned to CONV-002; it cannot authorize an expired consent or leak content
Logs and errors contain only identifiers and bounded outcome metadata

update_tasks.spec: Start from the exact accepted FOUND-LOCK-001 SHA, which must contain accepted QA-REPAIR-001, DATA-CORR-001, and CONTRACT-CORR-004 ancestry. Merge the exact accepted remote SHAs for EXPR-REPAIR-001, CONV-REPAIR-004, RESP-REPAIR-003, HAND-001, CARE-REPAIR-001, and PRIV-REPAIR-001 with clean --no-ff merges. Never merge or cherry-pick rejected EXPR-001, CONV-001, RESP-001, CARE-001, PRIV-001, QA-001, CONV-REPAIR-001, RESP-REPAIR-001, CONTRACT-CORR-002, CONTRACT-CORR-003, CONV-REPAIR-002, CONV-REPAIR-003, or RESP-REPAIR-002 commit objects. Add only integration-owned actor boundaries, command and query composition, routes, database wiring, and demo documentation. Preserve Fixture and non-production truth labels.
acceptance: FOUND-LOCK-001 is the exact integration base and QA-REPAIR-001, DATA-CORR-001, and CONTRACT-CORR-004 are verified ancestors
Every non-ancestor dependency SHA is an exact second parent of a clean no-ff merge
CONV-REPAIR-004 is the sole integrated conversation implementation and rejected CONV-REPAIR-003 is not an ancestor
HAND-001 remains the accepted handover implementation and is not repeated or replaced
No rejected or failed Attempt SHA is an ancestor of the integrated alpha
The seven-step Fixture flow runs through real command and query handlers and disposable PostgreSQL
Server-side authorization and pre-provider authorization remain effective
Blocked, denied, provider-failed, database-failed, care-boundary, deletion, and export paths remain explicit
Both browser viewports render the real Next.js application without regression
README and demo documentation distinguish Fixture, local runtime, public deployment, and official acceptance

update_tasks.spec: Harden the accepted CONV-REPAIR-004 capability after INT-001. Replace every Date.parse or epoch-millisecond consent comparison with the CONTRACT-CORR-004 package-root compareTimestamps function while retaining the general Clock Date adapter for non-care compatibility. Add sub-millisecond expiry, concurrent confirmation, double-submit, consent revocation during provider execution, source deletion, unauthorized ID guessing, provider failure, malformed output, and transactional rollback tests. Preserve the fail-closed disclosure skeleton and all user-facing conversation behavior.
acceptance: A consent decided at 2026-08-27T20:01:00.000998Z with expiry 2026-08-27T20:01:00.000999Z remains valid at the earlier instant and is invalid at equality or later
All consent ordering imports compareTimestamps from the contracts package root and contains no Date.parse or epoch-millisecond comparison
Concurrent confirmations and double submits create at most one shared signal
Consent revocation, source deletion, authorization drift, provider failure, malformed output, and transaction failure write nothing
The privacy skeleton continues to block repeated whitespace, punctuation, symbol, containment, and one-edit variants
No private content appears in logs, errors, reports, or unauthorized queries
